scenes.line1: How do you boost retrieval quality?
scenes.say: How do you make retrieval-augmented generation smarter and more relevant? What really boosts retrieval quality?

scenes.label: Chunking
scenes.sub: Split documents into smaller pieces, like 500 tokens each.
scenes.say: First, chunking splits documents into smaller, manageable pieces. For example, you might break them into sections of five hundred tokens.

rows.b: Find chunks similar to the query
Pick the best for LLM input

scenes.say: Next, reranking comes in. You retrieve chunks similar to your query, score each for relevance, and select the top ones for the language model.
Choosing chunk size matters. Small chunks give precision but can miss context. Large chunks offer more context but risk including irrelevant details.

scenes.question: Why not skip reranking?
scenes.right: Reranking ensures only the most relevant chunks reach the language model, improving response quality.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Why not skip reranking? Not all retrieved chunks are useful. Reranking makes sure only the most relevant ones reach the model.
